text.p: Malta strongly supports the idea of a single European currency which will have a major long-term impact on its economy, the Economic Services Minister Josef Bonnici said on Monday.

Speaking at a conference of the European Association of University Teachers of Banking and Finance, Bonnici said Malta was one of the foremost applicants in line for EU membership, and the adoption of a single European currency will be a grassroots change which will make a lasting impression on its economy.
Bonnici said the Malta government's overriding consideration was Malta's international competitiveness and currency stability was a priority in this context.
"All developments which may potentially lead to greater international stability in exchange movements is ultimately to our advantage," he said.

"Hence our enthusiasm for a single European currency. While appreciating the complex issues at stake for the larger European economies, no small or open economy can fail to support such an initiative whole-heartedly."
Earlier Bonnici outlined the progress the economy has made since 1987.
While other economies suffered at the hands of the latest recession, Malta's maintained a steady growth at an average of 5.5 per cent over the past 10 years.
Investment inflows reached record levels, unemployment declined to 3.5 per cent and inflation averaged between three and four per cent, Bonnici said.
